# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-6 (Extended v76)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; **Valjean ESCAPES from M. sur M. jail same evening Javert arrested him beside Fantine's death-bed**); December 1823 (Montfermeil tavern, Valjean rescued Cosette, paid Thénardier 1,500 francs); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 Spring onward (lodging at decrepit building; winter passed; spring advanced); **CURRENT TIME: Summer of second year (approximately 1825-1826), Summer night approximately 1-2 a.m. CURRENT LOCATION: Inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district; NOW ACHIEVED SANCTUARY BUT DISCOVERY OF ELDERLY FAUCHELEVENT AND CONVENT SETTING; JAVERT NOW IN PARIS WITH POLICE FORCE; TRACKING VALJEAN**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford (English harbor towns); Arras; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Paris (1823-1826) including Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, Jardin des Plantes. **Mouffetard quarter** (Rue Censier; Rue Copeau; Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor; Rue du Puits l'Ermite; Rue de Pontoise; commissary of police office No. 14; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont church). **Decrepit building (Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, numbered 50 outside/52 inside)**: Mean building appearing as hovel but large internally; first story contains numerous chambers and attics, occupied by old woman portress; rest uninhabited. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, walls and solitude; monkish aspect; roads unpaved. **RUE DROIT-MUR and RUE PETIT-PICPUS**: Bordered by mean houses and solitary severe building with numerous parts growing higher; angle descends to wall in deeply retreating niche concealed by two corners. **Wall (approximately 18 feet height)**: Extended from niche angle to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur to gloomy building. **Gloomy building (CONVENT)**: Severe, somber aspect; only one window heavily shuttered with sheet zinc; front has ancient cistern pipes and linden-tree with ivy above wall; interior façades tragic with all windows grated; upper story has scuttles resembling prison cells; casts shadow over garden; **CONTAINS CHOIR OF WOMEN'S VOICES—celestial hymn burst forth during night after Javert's patrol retreated, voices of virgins and innocent children, described as those heard by newborn infants and dying men**. **INTERIOR GARDEN (convent grounds)**: Vast oblong area with alley of large poplars at further end; tolerably tall forest trees in corners; unshaded space in centre with large solitary tree, gnarled fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well; stone benches; alleys bordered with gloomy shrubs; grass and green mould covered rest; roof of building descended from wooden barricade top to within short distance of ground with gentle slope grazing linden-tree; wall much higher on garden side; ground at very great depth below. **Hall inside building**: Vast paved with large flagstones, cut by arcades and pillars, lit by single taper in corner, deserted; **formerly contained mysterious form lying face downward with arms extended in cross and rope around neck—NOW IDENTIFIED AS ELEMENT OF FAUCHELEVENT'S GARDENING WORK (straw mat spreading operation)**. **Gardener's quarters**: Within convent buildings; contains bed where Cosette now sleeps; table with cheese, black bread, wine, glasses.

## Jean Valjean's Escape and Current Sanctuary (Summer Year 2—CONTINUING WITH REVELATION)
**ESCAPE FROM M. SUR M.**: Evening of day when Javert arrested him beside Fantine's death-bed, January 1823, Valjean escaped from town jail of M. sur M.; police supposed he went to Paris. **REFUGE DISCOVERY**: Successfully climbed 18-foot wall using muscular force alone; placed Cosette on back; discovered building roof descended to within short distance of ground; descended safely to interior garden; retrieved shoes; moved to shed with Cosette. **MYSTERIOUS BELL-SOUND RESOLVED**: Upon exploration, heard faint tinkling bell from garden; trembled believing Javert had posted watchers; sound accompanied by peculiar movements in melon patch area. **FAUCHELEVENT IDENTIFICATION AND REVELATION**: When Valjean encountered elderly man in garden, man revealed himself as old Fauchelevent, crippled gardener admitted to convent on Valjean's (then Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation two years previously (approximately 1821) after falling from cart. **BELL SOURCE EXPLAINED**: Bell and kneecap worn by Fauchelevent to mark his movements while spreading straw mats over melon beds—operation explained the peculiar movements Valjean observed from shed; bell hung on nail beside vintage basket in gardener's quarters after discovery. **PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE**: Profound truth deepening—so long as Cosette near him, he needs nothing except for her, fears nothing except for her; experiencing continual tremor; distrust of day and night equally. **COAT SACRIFICE**: Removed coat to cover Cosette; coat replaced after reaching safety. **CURRENT STATE**: Secured in convent sanctuary (location of **Convent of Petit-Picpus**, Quartier Saint-Antoine, where Fauchelevent works as gardener); wearing cravat and coat; hat recovered from over wall. **COSETTE SAFE**: Now sleeping in Fauchelevent's bed after warming by good fire; rosy again; completely dependent on Valjean.

## Fauchelevent (Elderly Gardener, NEW CHARACTER—ESTABLISHED ALLY)
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener; admitted to Convent of Petit-Picpus approximately two years previously (1821) on recommendation of Mayor Madeleine (Valjean) after falling from cart; now works as gardener in convent grounds. **Character**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; reproaches Valjean for not recognizing him immediately, calling him "Father Madeleine" and accusing him of ingratitude despite saving people's lives; speaks freely about his work and circumstances. **Current occupation and actions**: Spreading straw mats over melon beds in garden; wears bell and kneecap device marking his movements; bell tinkles with his approach and retreat, ceases when he halts; accompanied Valjean to his quarters. **Hospitality**: Provided Cosette safe bed; offered Valjean cheese, black bread, wine; warming themselves at table in his quarters. **Status**: Now Valjean's only known ally and protector in Paris; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's presence in convent sanctuary.

## Javert's Pursuit and Migration to Paris (CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT)
**ESCAPE AFTERMATH**: When Valjean escaped from M. sur M. jail evening of Fantine's death (January 1823), police supposed he went to Paris, described as "maelstrom where everything is lost," belly of the world, abyss where fugitives disappear in crowds. **JAVERT REASSIGNED**: Summoned to Paris to assist police researches on escaped fugitive; Javert had rendered powerful assistance in recapture of Valjean previously (at Fantine arrest/trial sequence); his zeal and intelligence remarked by M. Chabouillet, secretary of the Prefecture under Comte Anglès; Chabouillet (already Javert's patron) had inspector Javert of M. sur M. attached to police force of Paris circa 1823. **PARIS SERVICE**: Rendered himself useful in diverse honorable manners with Paris police; **no longer thought of Jean Valjean as wolf of yesterday forgotten when new wolf pursued**, until December 1823 when newspaper announced Jean Valjean's death in formal terms; Javert read name, confined himself to remark "That's a good entry," threw paper aside, thought no more about matter. **REACTIVATION**: Subsequently, police report transmitted from Seine-et-Oise prefecture concerning abduction of child Cosette in Montfermeil; report stated girl of seven or eight, entrusted to innkeeper, stolen by stranger; daughter of girl Fantine, died in hospital; **Javert's memory revived**—he recalled Fantine's name was well known to him; remembered Valjean had asked three-day respite to fetch Fantine's child; remembered Valjean arrested in Paris stepping into coach for Montfermeil; suspected Valjean had made previous excursion to Montfermeil searching for Fantine's daughter. **JAVERT'S DEDUCTION AND ACTION**: Understood now: Fantine's daughter was in Montfermeil; Valjean was seeking her; child now stolen by stranger—could that stranger be Jean Valjean? But Valjean was dead (believed from newspaper report). Without telling anyone, Javert took coach from Pewter Platter tavern, Cul-de-Sac de la Planchette, made trip to Montfermeil. **GORBEAU HOUSE INVESTIGATION**: Followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; got old woman portress talking; she confirmed coat lined with millions episode and thousand-franc bill; Javert hired room, installed himself evening same day; came and listened at mysterious lodger's door hoping catch sound of voice; Valjean saw his candle through key-hole, foiled spy by keeping silent. **PURSUIT ESCALATION**: On following day Valjean noticed five-franc piece falling; old woman heard rattling coin, suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; at night when Valjean came out, Javert waited behind trees of boulevard with two men. **CURRENT STATUS**: Javert actively pursuing Valjean in Paris; stationed in surveillance positions awaiting fugitive.

## English Harbor Towns Communities (SECONDARY SETTING—INTEGRATED INTO NARRATIVE FLOW)
Named residents include: Ismira Stenson (fell asleep in chair before fire caught); Pelde Stenson (counted coins twice, came up penny short); Harine Lindmere (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Davus Stenworth and Havus Stenworth (remarked river up, water swelling in spring); Yera (read almanac aloud, mispronouncing saints); Orrald the Younger (received confidence, swore to teach children of Elmhaven letters); Harine (complained of aching back); Orrald (bought ribbon, regretted it); Harine and Havus (talked of weather, harvest, lame horse).
